newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms John Mowlem ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms John Mowlem ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Tuesday it had affirmed John Mowlem & Company Plc (Mowlem) ratings at BB long-term and B short-term.
"At the onset of recession in 1989/90, Mowlem was caught with high levels of debt following substantial expansion in the late 1980s," IBCA said in a statement.
"The subsequent reorganisation and disposal programme, initiated in order to reduce borrowings, has resulted in extensive one-off costs and has absorbed management time."
"Meanwhile, the UK construction market has been fiercely competitive due to weak demand and an excess number of participants," IBCA said.
It said Mowlem finally sold London City Airport in October last year, realising a loss on the disposal of 5.5 million stg but eliminating a future drain on resources.
"The long-running Carlton Gate legal battle, dating back to 1990, was also ended in 1995 with a 14 million stg agreed settlement, paid in Q196," IBCA said.

"Mowlem is now beginning to show signs of having turned the corner. The group has redefined its approach to construction, focusing on more remunerative regional work through its extensive national network, while avoiding the more competitive high profile projects unless an acceptable margin can be achieved," the agency said.

"Its Access Products & Services division, including SGB ladders and scaffolding, is performing well and may be partially floated in the near future. The growth areas for the group are the service-based divisions, Facilities Management and Environmental Services," said IBCA. "With this new focus on construction-based activities in its wider sense and assuming a partial divestment of SGB, Mowlem's exposure to capital intensive businesses would be much reduced."
IBCA said if the construction division managed the forecast recovery from a first half loss of 0.9 million stg, then all Mowlem's activities would be profitable by the year-end.
